spots.name: Krasny Avenue
spots.summary: Krasny Prospekt or Krasny Avenue is the central street and major thoroughfare in the city of Novosibirsk, Russia. Until 1920, it was known as the Nikolaevsky Prospekt or Nicholas' Avenue. Its length is about 7 km.

spots.name: Novosibirsk Opera and Ballet Theatre
spots.summary: The Novosibirsk Opera and Ballet Theatre, officially the Novosibirsk State Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre, is a theatre in Novosibirsk and Siberia. It is located at the center of Novosibirsk at Lenin square.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is the Eastern Orthodox Cathedral in Novosibirsk, Russia, named in honor of Saint Alexander Nevsky.

names.zh: 亞歷山大涅夫斯基大教堂

spots.name: Novosibirsk railway station
spots.summary: Novosibirsk–Glavny is the primary passenger railway station for the city of Novosibirsk in Russia, and an important stop along the Trans-Siberian Railway and Turkestan–Siberia Railway. The station is one of the largest in Russia. The main building takes an area of 30,000 square metres.

spots.name: 100-Flat Building
spots.summary: The 100-Flat Building is an eight-floor residential building in Novosibirsk, Russia, located at Krasny Prospekt, 16. It is a historical and cultural monument of federal significance in Russia. The building was created in 1934–1937 by prominent Russian architects Andrey Kryachkov and Vitaly Maslennikov.

spots.name: Novosibirsk State Museum of Local Lore
spots.summary: History of Novosibirsk and Siberia and its peoples from mammoth-hunting days through Russian colonisation, the coming of the railway, communism, and today. Audioguide via izi.travel app. Temporary exhibitions on the top floor.

spots.summary: Saint Nicholas Chapel is a Russian Orthodox chapel in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia.

spots.name: Central Siberian Botanic Garden
spots.summary: Central Siberian Botanic Garden is a botanic garden in the south-eastern part of Novosibirsk, Russia. It borders with Akademgorodok.

spots.name: Lenin Square, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: Lenin Square is the main square of Novosibirsk, located in the Tsentralny City District. It consists of Transport and Theater squares.

spots.name: Novosibirsk Conservatory
spots.summary: Novosibirsk State Conservatory named after M. I. Glinka is an educational music institution in Novosibirsk, Russia. It was founded in 1956.

names.ru: Новосибирская государственная консерватория имени М. И. Глинки

names.zh: 新西伯利亚国立音乐学院

spots.name: Monument to the Heroes of the Revolution
spots.summary: The Monument to the Heroes of the Revolution is a memorial located in the very center of Novosibirsk, Russia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Monument to the Heroes of the Revolution

spots.name: Karl Marx Square Water Tower
spots.summary: Karl Marx Square Water Tower is a water tower in Leninsky District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It was built in 1939.

spots.name: City Trade House
spots.summary: City Trade House is a building in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It is located at Krasny Avenue. The building was designed by architect Andrey Kryachkov.

spots.name: Globus Theatre
spots.summary: Novosibirsk Globus Theatre is a theatre in Novosibirsk city, Siberia, Russia.

spots.name: House of Lenin
spots.summary: House of Lenin, currently Philharmonic Chamber hall, is a building in Novosibirsk, located at Krasniy Prospect, 32. C.

spots.name: Serebrennikovskaya Street
spots.summary: Serebrennikovskaya Street is a street in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It runs south-north. The street starts from the Altay Railway Overpass and ends near the southern facade of the Novosibirsk Opera and Ballet Theatre.

spots.name: Gosbank Building, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: The Gosbank Building is a constructivist building designed by Andrey Kryachkov. It is located on Krasny Avenue in Novosibirsk, Russia. The building is a part of the architectural ensemble of Lenin Square.

spots.name: Lenin Street
spots.summary: Lenin Street is a street in Tsentralny and Zheleznodorozhny districts of Novosibirsk, Russia.

spots.name: Business House, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: Business House is a constructivist building in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It is located on the corner of Krasny Avenue and Lenin Street. The building is a part of the architectural ensemble of Lenin Square. It was built in 1928. Architects: D. F. Fridman, I. A. Burlakov.

spots.name: October Revolution House of Culture
spots.summary: October Revolution House of Culture is a constructivist building in Zheleznodorozhny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It was built in 1927. The building is located on the corner of Lenin and Revolution streets. Architect: I. A. Burlakov.

spots.name: Sovetskaya Street
spots.summary: Sovetskaya Street is a street in Novosibirsk, Russia. It branches off from Krasny Avenue near the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and then runs north parallel to it. Sovetskaya Street ends at the intersection with Zheleznodorozhnaya and Pisarev streets.

spots.name: Kryukov House
spots.summary: Kryukov House is a building in Zheleznodorozhny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia, built in 1908. It is located on the corner of Sovetskaya and Gorky streets. The house originally belonged to the merchant Zakhary Grigoryevich Kryukov.

spots.name: Gorky Street
spots.summary: Maxim Gorky Street is an east–west street in Zheleznodorozhny and Tsentralny districts of Novosibirsk, Russia.

spots.name: Deputatskaya Street
spots.summary: Deputatskaya Street is a street in Zheleznodorozhny and Tsentralny districts of Novosibirsk, Russia. It consists of two fragments. The first fragment crosses Street of Revolution and forms a T-intersection with Uritsky Street.

spots.name: Ordzhonikidze Street
spots.summary: Ordzhonikidze Street is a street in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. The street runs from the intersection with Vokzalnaya Magistral and Sovetskaya Street, crosses Krasny Avenue, Kamenskaya, Shamshin Family streets and connects with Trudovaya Lane.

spots.name: Main Post Office, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: Main Post Office is a building in Zheleznodorozhny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It is located on the corner of Lenin and Sovetskaya streets. The building was built in 1916. Architect: Andrey Kryachkov.

names.ru: Государственный концертный зал имени Арнольда Каца

spots.name: Building of State Institutions
spots.summary: Building of State Institutions is a building in Tsentralny District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It is located on the corner of Krasny Prospekt and Ordzhonikidze Street. The building was built in 1924–1925 by architect Andrey Kryachkov. In the 1930s, it was reconstructed by S. I. Ignatovich.

spots.name: Sibrevcom Street
spots.summary: Sibrevcom Street is a west–east street in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It runs from a T-intersection with Krasny Avenue, crosses Serebrennikovskaya Street and ends near the Sibrevcomovsky Bridge over Ippodromskaya Street.

names.ru: Доходный дом мещанина А. Ф. Выходцева

spots.name: Water Tower No. 2
spots.summary: Water Tower No. 2 is an octagonal water tower in Zheleznodorozhny District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It was built in 1902.

spots.name: City Primary School on Lenin Street, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: City Primary School on Lenin Street is a building in Zheleznodorozhny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It was constructed in 1912. Architect: Andrey Kryachkov. The building is located on the corner of Lenin Street and Street of Revolution.
spots.wikipediaTitle: City Primary School on Lenin Street, Novosibirsk

spots.name: Soyuzzoloto House
spots.summary: Soyuzzoloto Residential House is a constructivist building in Tsentralny City District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It is located on the corner of Kamenskaya and Oktyabrskaya streets. The building was constructed in 1932. Architects: A. I. Bobrov, B. A. Gordeyev.

spots.name: Stanislavsky Street 7, Novosibirsk
spots.summary: Stanislavsky Street 7 is a residential building in Leninsky District of Novosibirsk, Russia. It was built in 1940. Architects: V. M. Teitel, A. V. Baransky.
